items.mainDefect: The server never de-duplicates the submitted guest list, so case-variant duplicates such as a@x.com and A@x.com are both inserted as attendees.

secondary.defect: The filter compares guests to existing attendee emails case-sensitively, so a case-variant of an existing attendee gets added again.

items.mainDefect: Guest emails are checked against the lowercased blacklist without being lowercased themselves, so changing the case of an email bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

secondary.defect: The case-sensitive guest === attendee.email check lets a case-variant of an existing attendee get past the duplicate filter and be inserted.

items.mainDefect: The server does not enforce uniqueness within the submitted guest array, so createMany can insert identical emails more than once.

secondary.defect: Attendees are read and later written with no transaction, so two concurrent addGuests calls can both pass the filter. This either inserts duplicates or throws an unhandled Prisma P2002 error.

items.mainDefect: uniqueGuests never de-duplicates the input array, and the server schema has no uniqueness check, so the same email in the input creates two attendee rows and two emails.

secondary.defect: Guests are compared raw against the lowercased blacklist, so an uppercase variant of a blacklisted email is added and emailed.
The case-sensitive === comparison against existing attendees lets a case-variant duplicate an existing attendee.
